haiku-low.q1: Only a SHA-256 hash (token_hash) is persisted. Plaintext exists only in server memory during create, the 201 response, the browser dialog, and the client's secret store.
haiku-low.q2: They cannot get it back. The browser drops the token when the dialog closes, and the server never shows it again. Revoke it and create a new one.
haiku-low.q3: The request gets 409 token_limit_reached with the message "Revoke a token before creating a new one." Nothing is created.
haiku-low.q4: On the first request that starts after the revoke commits, which gets 401. A request that already passed the token check may still finish.
haiku-low.q5: Unknown, revoked and expired tokens all get the same 401 with {"error":"invalid_token"} and the same WWW-Authenticate header. The reason is only in internal logs.
haiku-low.q6: It hashes the token with SHA-256 and looks up token_hash on the primary every request. Postgres computes is_active: revoked_at is null and expires_at is later than now().
haiku-low.q7: A request whose row shows needs_touch (last_used_at null or older than 55 minutes) triggers an UPDATE setting last_used_at to now(). Postgres's clock and that 55-minute rule limit it to one write per token.
haiku-low.q8: The API request still succeeds. The failure is logged, and the next request tries the write again.
haiku-low.q9: It sets revoked_at to now() if it is null. The row stays for audit, and inactive rows drop out of the list and the limit count.
haiku-low.q10: Another user's id gets the same 404 "Token not found." as a nonexistent id. Revoking an already-revoked token is idempotent: revoked_at is kept and retrying is safe.
haiku-low.q11: An active token exists and counts toward the limit, but no one holds its plaintext. The page reloads the list: if the name appears, revoke it and recreate; otherwise, try again.

sonnet.q1: It stores only the SHA-256 hash of the full token string (including pat_) in api_tokens.token_hash. Plaintext exists only in server memory during the create request, the 201 response, the browser dialog while open, and wherever the user pastes it (e.g. the client's secret store).
sonnet.q2: They can't. The token is shown once and the server keeps no copy and won't show it again. They must revoke it and create a new one.
sonnet.q3: The server rolls back and returns 409 token_limit_reached. The browser shows: "You have 10 active tokens. Revoke a token before creating a new one."
sonnet.q4: On the next request that starts after the revoke commits, which gets 401. A request that had already passed the token check before the commit may still finish.
sonnet.q5: All get the same 401 with body {"error":"invalid_token"} and the same headers (WWW-Authenticate: Bearer). The responses do not differ; the reason is only in internal logs.
sonnet.q6: It computes SHA-256 of the presented token and looks up api_tokens by token_hash on the primary DB. Postgres computes is_active (revoked_at is null and expires_at later than now(), using its own clock); the record is usable only if is_active is true.
sonnet.q7: An authenticated API call where Postgres reports needs_touch true (last_used_at is null or older than 55 minutes) triggers UPDATE last_used_at = now(). That 55-minute threshold, decided by Postgres, limits it to at most one write per token per 55 minutes.
sonnet.q8: The failure is logged and the request is still served normally (2xx). The next request tries the write again.
sonnet.q9: It sets revoked_at = COALESCE(revoked_at, now()) on the row; the row is kept for audit. Revoked rows are inactive, so they drop out of the token list (and the 10-token limit count).
sonnet.q10: Another user's token id: the UPDATE matches 0 rows (it filters by user_id), so 404 is returned, same as for a nonexistent token, with message "Token not found." Already-revoked own token: revoke is idempotent via COALESCE, so it succeeds (204) without changing revoked_at.
sonnet.q11: If the COMMIT happened, a token exists and counts toward the limit but nobody holds the plaintext and it can't be shown again. The page says it could not confirm creation, reloads the list; if a token with that name is listed, the user is told to revoke it and create a new one; if not, told it wasn't created and to try again. Retrying without revoking gets 409 name_taken with an explanatory message.
